entities.summary: The German destroyer Z4 Richard Beitzen was one of four Type 1934 destroyers built for the German Navy (Kriegsmarine) during the mid-1930s. Completed in 1937, the ship spent most of her time training although she did participate in the occupation of Memel in early 1939. At the beginning of World War II in September 1939, the ship was initially deployed to blockade the Polish coast, but was soon transferred to the Kattegat where she inspected neutral shipping for contraband goods. In late 1939 and early 1940, the ship laid two offensive minefields off the English coast that claimed 17 merchant ships.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The German destroyer Z4 Richard Beitzen played a role in laying minefields off the English coast that claimed 17 merchant ships, contributing to the start of World War II. Although its impact was limited to regional conflict, it remains notable for its involvement in one of the war's early naval operations.
